name: India Gate
description: A 42-metre war memorial arch on Kartavya Path, completed in 1931 to honour Indian soldiers of the First World War. The lawns around it are busiest in the evening.

name: Red Fort
description: Shah Jahan's red-sandstone palace-fortress, completed in 1648 as the seat of Mughal power. A UNESCO World Heritage Site with small museums inside its walls.

name: Qutub Minar
description: A 73-metre minaret begun at the end of the 12th century, standing in a complex of early Sultanate monuments that also holds the Iron Pillar of Delhi.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: The garden tomb of the Mughal emperor Humayun, completed in the 1570s. A forerunner of the Taj Mahal and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Lotus Temple
description: A Bahá'í House of Worship shaped like a white lotus flower, opened in 1986 and open to people of every faith for silent prayer.

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
description: A large Hindu temple complex opened in 2005, known for its intricately carved central monument, gardens and evening water show.

name: Jama Masjid
description: One of India's largest mosques, built by Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656. Visitors are not admitted during the midday prayer break.

name: Chandni Chowk
description: Old Delhi's main bazaar since the 17th century, with spice, fabric and sweet shops spilling into narrow side lanes.

name: National Museum
description: One of India's largest museums, with collections from the Harappan civilisation to Buddhist art, miniature paintings and decorative arts.

name: Lodhi Garden
description: A large city park built around 15th- and 16th-century tombs of the Sayyid and Lodi dynasties. Popular for early-morning walks.

name: Raj Ghat
description: A black-marble memorial platform beside the Yamuna marking where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated in 1948, set in quiet lawns.

name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
description: A prominent Sikh gurdwara with a golden dome and a sacred pool. Its community kitchen serves free meals to every visitor.

name: Jantar Mantar
description: An 18th-century observatory built by Maharaja Jai Singh II, with giant masonry instruments for measuring time and the positions of stars.

name: Agrasen ki Baoli
description: A 60-metre-long medieval stepwell with 108 steps, hidden among the office towers of central New Delhi.

name: Safdarjung's Tomb
description: A sandstone and marble garden tomb built in 1754, often described as the last great Mughal garden tomb.

name: Hauz Khas Complex
description: A medieval reservoir surrounded by a 14th-century madrasa and tombs, beside a lake, a deer park and the cafés of Hauz Khas Village.

name: Purana Qila
description: One of Delhi's oldest forts, rebuilt by Sher Shah Suri and Humayun in the 16th century, with a boating lake below its walls.

name: Sunder Nursery
description: A restored 16th-century garden next to Humayun's Tomb, with heritage monuments, a bonsai house and landscaped lawns.

name: Dilli Haat (INA)
description: An open-air crafts bazaar and food court where artisans and cooks from different Indian states run stalls.

name: Taj Mahal
description: The white-marble mausoleum Shah Jahan built for Mumtaz Mahal on the bank of the Yamuna, completed around 1653. A UNESCO World Heritage Site, closed on Fridays.

name: Agra Fort
description: A massive red-sandstone fort rebuilt by Akbar from 1565, later given marble palaces by Shah Jahan that look across the river to the Taj.

name: Itmad-ud-Daulah
description: A jewel-like marble tomb with fine stone inlay, built in the 1620s by Nur Jahan for her father and often called the 'Baby Taj'.

name: Mehtab Bagh
description: A Mughal garden on the opposite bank of the Yamuna, aligned with the Taj Mahal and known for sunset views of it.

name: Akbar's Tomb
description: The tomb of the emperor Akbar at Sikandra, completed in 1613 in a large walled garden where blackbuck graze.

name: Jama Masjid
description: A red-sandstone congregational mosque completed in 1648 near Agra Fort, dedicated to Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara.

name: Chini Ka Rauza
description: The 17th-century riverside tomb of the scholar-poet Afzal Khan Shirazi, notable for the remains of its glazed tile work.

name: Ram Bagh
description: Believed to be one of the oldest Mughal gardens in India, first laid out by Babur in the 1520s on the Yamuna's east bank.

name: Mariam's Tomb
description: The tomb of Mariam-uz-Zamani, wife of Akbar and mother of Jahangir, a short walk from Akbar's own tomb at Sikandra.

name: Kinari Bazaar
description: A dense old-city market behind the Jama Masjid, known for wedding trimmings, textiles, jewellery and street food.

name: Gurudwara Guru ka Taal
description: A Sikh gurdwara at a site associated with Guru Tegh Bahadur, built around a 17th-century water reservoir, with a langar open to all.

name: Soami Bagh Samadh
description: The white-marble memorial of the founder of the Radhasoami faith, a carved temple whose construction has continued for over a century.

name: Sur Sarovar Bird Sanctuary
description: A wetland bird sanctuary around Keetham Lake on the Agra-Delhi highway, best in winter when migratory birds arrive.

name: Amber Fort
description: A hilltop fort-palace of the Kachwaha Rajputs above Maota Lake, famous for its mirror-work Sheesh Mahal. Part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

name: City Palace
description: The royal residence at the heart of the old city, mixing Rajput and Mughal styles, with museums of textiles, arms and royal objects.

name: Hawa Mahal
description: The 'Palace of Winds' (1799): a five-storey pink-sandstone façade of 953 small windows that let royal women watch the street unseen.

name: Jantar Mantar
description: A UNESCO-listed observatory completed in 1734 by Jai Singh II, home to the world's largest stone sundial.

name: Jal Mahal
description: A palace that seems to float in Man Sagar Lake. It is viewed from the lakeside promenade rather than visited inside.

name: Nahargarh Fort
description: An 18th-century fort on the Aravalli ridge above Jaipur, with a palace of identical royal suites and wide views over the city.

name: Jaigarh Fort
description: A fortress above Amber built to protect it, home to Jaivana, one of the largest wheeled cannons ever made.

name: Albert Hall Museum
description: Rajasthan's oldest museum, in an Indo-Saracenic building opened in 1887, with miniatures, carpets, armour and an Egyptian mummy.

name: Birla Mandir
description: A white-marble temple to Lakshmi and Narayan, built in 1988 at the foot of Moti Dungri hill. Closed for a few hours in the afternoon.

name: Galtaji Temple
description: An old pilgrimage site in a rocky gorge east of the city, with temples, spring-fed water tanks and many resident monkeys.

name: Patrika Gate
description: A brightly painted gateway at Jawahar Circle whose arches and pillars illustrate the regions and crafts of Rajasthan.

name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
description: A much-visited Krishna temple in the City Palace complex, open in morning and evening darshan sessions.

name: Panna Meena ka Kund
description: A 16th-century stepwell near Amber with symmetrical criss-cross staircases, a favourite with photographers.

name: Johari Bazaar
description: The old city's jewellers' market, known for gemstones, silver and block-printed textiles under arcaded pink façades.

name: Sisodia Rani Garden
description: A terraced 18th-century garden and palace built by Sawai Jai Singh II for his Sisodia queen, decorated with murals.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of the most revered Shiva temples in India, reached through the Kashi Vishwanath corridor that links it to the Ganga ghats.

name: Dashashwamedh Ghat (Ganga Aarti)
description: The busiest ghat on the Ganga, where priests perform the choreographed Ganga Aarti with lamps every evening. Its visit window follows the aarti.

name: Assi Ghat
description: The southernmost major ghat, popular for sunrise, boat rides and a more relaxed riverside atmosphere.

name: Sarnath (Dhamek Stupa)
description: Where the Buddha gave his first sermon after enlightenment. The Dhamek Stupa and monastery ruins stand in a landscaped archaeological park.

name: Manikarnika Ghat
description: The principal cremation ghat of Varanasi, central to the city's beliefs about liberation. Visitors should observe respectfully and avoid photography.

name: Ramnagar Fort
description: An 18th-century sandstone fort on the east bank of the Ganga, home of the Maharaja of Benares, with a museum of vintage cars, arms and clocks.

name: Bharat Kala Bhavan
description: A university museum on the Banaras Hindu University campus with rich collections of paintings, sculpture, textiles and archaeology.

name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
description: A popular Hanuman temple associated with the poet-saint Tulsidas, especially crowded on Tuesdays and Saturdays.

name: Durga Kund Temple
description: An 18th-century red-painted temple of the goddess Durga beside a large stepped water tank.

name: Tulsi Manas Mandir
description: A white-marble temple opened in 1964 at the place where Tulsidas is believed to have written the Ramcharitmanas, whose verses line its walls.

name: New Vishwanath Temple (BHU)
description: A tall white-marble Shiva temple on the Banaras Hindu University campus, open to all and calmer than the old-city temples.

name: Sarnath Archaeological Museum
description: The Archaeological Survey of India's oldest site museum, home to the Lion Capital of Ashoka, India's national emblem.

name: Kaal Bhairav Temple
description: An old temple of Kaal Bhairav, regarded as the guardian deity (kotwal) of Varanasi.
